parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.lead:
Fig. 7.1 shows the circuit diagram containing an operational amplifier (op-amp).

[[fig:f1]]
parts.text: State the name of this type of amplifier.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the gain of the amplifier is 6.0.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
At time *t* = 0 the input potential *V*ᵢₙ is zero. *V*ᵢₙ then gradually increases with time *t* as shown in Fig. 7.2.

[[fig:f2]]

On Fig. 7.2 sketch a line to show the variation with time *t* of the output potential *V*ₒᵤₜ from time *t* = 0 to time *t* = *T*.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text: State how the circuit of Fig. 7.1 may be changed so that the gain of the amplifier is dependent on light intensity.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: An op-amp is to be used to switch on a high-voltage heater.
parts.text: State the name of the component used as the output device of the op-amp.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Complete Fig. 7.3 using the device name in (i) and a diode so that the heater may be switched on when the output of the op-amp is positive.

[[fig:f3]]

figures.caption: Fig. 7.1
figures.alt: Circuit diagram of an operational amplifier with 3.6 kΩ and 0.72 kΩ resistors, ±3.0 V supplies, and input and output potentials.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.2
figures.alt: A gridded graph of potential in volts against time, with a straight line increasing from zero to about one volt.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.3
figures.alt: An incomplete op-amp circuit with input connections, a grounded lower rail, and two terminals marked for connections to a high-voltage heater.
